description: Optional keywords must be exactly that - optional. Each test here runs the same query with and without the optional token (or with the defaults spelled out) and pins BOTH the rows of each spelling and their equivalence: INNER on a join, OUTER on LEFT and FULL, ASC / NULLS LAST and DESC / NULLS FIRST as the ORDER BY defaults, TEMP as the abbreviation of TEMPORARY, and FLATTEN's outer / recursive / mode defaults written out in full. UNION is the counter-example that belongs with them: it is the one optional keyword that CHANGES semantics, so it is pinned from the other side - without ALL the default is DISTINCT and the row goes away. File-level coverage elsewhere exercises each SPELLING; this suite pins the EQUIVALENCE. Converted 1:1 from query/OptionalKeywordEquivalenceTest (now retired); the Java compared two result sets cell by cell in a loop, so each converted test asserts the ordered rows of both spellings, which is the same claim made checkable without the loop.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE a (k INTEGER, av VARCHAR)
CREATE TABLE b (k INTEGER, bv VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO a VALUES (1, 'a1'), (2, 'a2'), (3, 'a3')
INSERT INTO b VALUES (2, 'b2'), (3, 'b3'), (4, 'b4')
SELECT a.k, av, bv FROM a JOIN b ON b.k = a.k ORDER BY a.k
SELECT a.k, av, bv FROM a INNER JOIN b ON b.k = a.k ORDER BY a.k
SELECT a.k, av, bv FROM a LEFT JOIN b ON b.k = a.k ORDER BY a.k
SELECT a.k, av, bv FROM a LEFT OUTER JOIN b ON b.k = a.k ORDER BY a.k
SELECT a.k, b.k, av, bv FROM a FULL JOIN b ON b.k = a.k ORDER BY a.k NULLS LAST, b.k
SELECT a.k, b.k, av, bv FROM a FULL OUTER JOIN b ON b.k = a.k ORDER BY a.k NULLS LAST, b.k
CREATE TABLE n (v INTEGER)
INSERT INTO n VALUES (2), (NULL), (1)
SELECT v FROM n ORDER BY v
SELECT v FROM n ORDER BY v ASC NULLS LAST
SELECT v FROM n ORDER BY v DESC
SELECT v FROM n ORDER BY v DESC NULLS FIRST
CREATE TEMP TABLE t_short (x INTEGER)
CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE t_long (x INTEGER)
INSERT INTO t_short VALUES (1)
INSERT INTO t_long VALUES (1)
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t_short
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t_long
CREATE TABLE j (v VARIANT)
INSERT INTO j SELECT PARSE_JSON('{"xs": [1, 2, 3]}')
SELECT f.value::INTEGER FROM j, LATERAL FLATTEN(input => v:xs) f ORDER BY 1
SELECT f.value::INTEGER FROM j, LATERAL FLATTEN(input => v:xs, outer => FALSE, recursive => FALSE, mode => 'BOTH') f ORDER BY 1
CREATE TABLE a (k INTEGER, av VARCHAR)
CREATE TABLE b (k INTEGER, bv VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO a VALUES (1, 'a1'), (2, 'a2'), (3, 'a3')
INSERT INTO b VALUES (2, 'b2'), (3, 'b3'), (4, 'b4')
SELECT k FROM a WHERE k <= 2 UNION SELECT k FROM b WHERE k <= 2 ORDER BY k
SELECT k FROM a WHERE k <= 2 UNION ALL SELECT k FROM b WHERE k <= 2 ORDER BY k
